chunks: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan, from Bakr ibn Salih, from al-Hasan ibn Sa'id, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Khazzaz and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, who said:

We entered upon Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) and we told him that Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) had seen his Lord in the form of a well-proportioned young man of approximately thirty years of age. And we said that Hisham ibn Salim, Sahib al-Taq, and al-Maysami say that He is hollow to the navel and the rest is Samad (not hollow).

So he fell prostrating to God, then said: 'Glory be to You! They have not recognised You, nor have they declared Your Oneness; it is for this reason that they have described You (in such terms). Glory be to You! Had they truly recognised You, they would have described You with what You have described Yourself. Glory be to You! How could their souls incline them to liken You to others?! O God! I do not describe You except with what You have described Yourself, nor do I liken You to Your creation. You are worthy of every good; so do not place me among the wrongdoing people.'
Then he turned towards us and said: 'Whatever you can imagine as a thing, conceive of God as other than it.'

Then he said: 'We, the family of Muhammad, are the middle path — the extremist cannot reach us, nor can the follower outpace us. O Muhammad! Indeed the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), when he looked at the Majesty of his Lord, was in the likeness of a well-proportioned young man of approximately thirty years of age. O Muhammad! My Lord, Mighty and Majestic, is far too exalted to be in the description of created beings.'

He (the narrator) said: I said, 'May I be your ransom! Whose legs were in greenness?' He said: 'That was Muhammad. When he looked at his Lord with his heart, He placed him in a light like the light of the Veils, until what was within the Veils became clear to him. The light of God — part of it is green, part of it is red, part of it is white, and part of it is other than that. O Muhammad! Whatever the Book (Quran) and the Sunnah testify for Him, we are the speakers of it.'

key_terms.الصَّمَدُ: Samad — Quranic attribute (112:2) meaning the Eternal, the Absolute, the One upon Whom all depend, commonly understood in classical theology as 'not hollow'
key_terms.النَّمَطُ الْأَوْسَطُ: The middle path — the Imam's description of Ahl al-Bayt as occupying the correct theological middle between extremism (ghuluww) and falling short (taqsir)
key_terms.الْحُجُبُ: al-Hujub — the Divine Veils; a theological concept referring to the screens of light between God and His creation
key_terms.سُبْحَانَكَ: Glory be to You — a formula of divine transcendence (tanzih), affirming God's absolute freedom from all deficiencies and creaturely attributes

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Rida say about describing God and the Prophet's vision of his Lord?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) was visited by two narrators who relayed a report that the Prophet Muhammad had seen God in the form of a young man, and that some prominent Shia scholars — Hisham ibn Salim, Sahib al-Taq (Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Nu'man), and al-Maysami — were describing God as physically hollow. The Imam immediately prostrated and offered a supplication of divine transcendence (tanzih), declaring that those who anthropomorphize God have neither truly recognized Him nor properly affirmed His Oneness. He then provided the authoritative clarification: the prophetic vision was of a form in which the Prophet appeared, not of God Himself, and that God is absolutely beyond all creaturely description. The Imam's teaching that 'whatever you can imagine as a thing, conceive of God as other than it' became a foundational principle of Shia Islamic theology.
word_analysis: the extremist/one who goes to excess
